entry.title: I’m a Front End Web Developer Learning Machine Learning From Scratch
entry.summary:
Hey, I'm a web developer - building UIs with React, TypeScript, Tailwind, and modern web tools. A few months ago, I decided to step into Machine Learning. Week 1: Building the Math Foundation Linear Algebra (vectors, matrices, eigenvalues) Calculus (derivatives, partial derivatives, gradients) Probability & Statistics Concept: Why Gradients Matter (w = w - learning_rate * gradient)
Repeat until you reach the minimum. Weeks 2–3: Supervised Learning (The Real Fun Begins) Linear & multiple linear regression Logistic regression for classification Cost functions, gradient descent, regularization, feature scaling, softmax I built small projects in Colab: House price predictor (linear regression) Spam email classifier (logistic regression) Concept: Regularization Weeks 4–5: Neural Networks & Tree Ensembles Built my first neural networks in TensorFlow (forward propagation + backpropagation) Learned decision trees, Random Forests, and XGBoost Concept: Backpropagation why the prediction was wrong and updates every weight accordingly using the chain rule. It’s like tracing a bug through a chain of React components — but for thousands of parameters. What Surprised Me Most The math finally made sense when I saw it used in real models. Building small projects > passive watching. ML and web development are a powerful combination — I can already imagine turning these models into real web features. What’s Next? More neural network practice Full mini-projects Course 3 (Unsupervised learning) I’ll be sharing regular updates here — code, lessons, and notebooks. If you’re also learning ML as a web developer, drop a comment. I’d love to hear your journey too!

entry.title: Google just redesigned the search box for the first time in 25 years — here’s why it matters more than you think.
entry.summary: For a quarter century, the Google search box has been one of the most recognizable interfaces in computing: a thin white rectangle, a blinking cursor, a few typed words, and a list of blue links.
